name: Reconstructed narrow two-story store on Dearborn Street, as Gifford draws it

documented_range.note: Drawn standing beside the first Tremont House (1833-1839) in Gifford's retrospective view of its street; taken as standing on 1 July 1835 on the owner's reading of the drawing (T-3605). No dated record of this building is known.

position.symbolic_location: Dearborn Street, dearborn west lake to alley: drawn store R4 of Gifford's row
position.note: Placed in the drawn order along the face, at stations 34.62-40.22 m of the face line (The block's Dearborn Street face, from the Lake corner north; the row stands on the line of the Tremont House's Dearborn side.), with 0.18 m between neighbours. Drawn at x 1445-1505 px of the 1637 px plate. The face is the drawing's (read through the Tremont's solved camera, data/reconstruction/1835_gifford_street_faces.json camera); the station is fitted, not measured.

derivation.reason: The drawing has no scale; the rows are fitted to the platted face.

footprint.note: 5.60 m of frontage proportioned from the drawn bays (gifford_tremont_house_no_1; the drawing's frontage stands over the C3 typology's own where the two differ), and 11.00 m deep, a depth the C3 typology allows. Neither is a measurement.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 4.5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn on this record's stable key from the stocks its household class may hang (4.5 in or 5 in; T-1839, docs/LIBERTIES.md L352), then advanced within them so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

occupants.note: SEATED BY THE STREET-FACE ADOPTION POLICY (docs/STREET-FACE-ADOPTION.md, the owner's ruling of 2026-08-29 for T-0354, extended 2026-08-30 for T-0416; liberty L212). The newspaper register places this business on Dearborn Street AND NOTHING NARROWER — 1 printing, 1835-08-19 to 1835-08-19, claims chicago_democrat_1835_08_19#c011 — so it takes the STREET FACE and not a lot. THE ROOF ENDS ITS PLATTED TIER AGAINST Dearborn Street, so it is a corner building and stands on that street as well as on the one its lot faces — the owner's ruling of 2026-08-30 (T-0416). Nothing about the roof changed and no geometry was raised to seat this business. WHICH roof on that face it is given is an allocation by tools/adopt_street_faces.py and not a reading of any source, and nothing here says this business stood nearer the corner than any other on the same face. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption: the business is documented, the building under it is not, and this attribute is graded `reconstructed` because the invented part is the whole of the placement.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED FROM A PICTURE. Gifford draws this store in the row beside the first Tremont House; the owner ruled on 2026-11-15 that the drawing is a reasonable view of 1835 and the street is to be built to it. The drawn form is read off the drawing and graded reconstructed; the building's presence in July 1835, its exact frontage and its station are reconstructed. Its occupants, if any, are dealt by the town's housing tools and graded by their own records.
